speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what the vertigo feels like—is it a sensation of the room spinning, or more of a feeling of lightheadedness? Did these symptoms start suddenly while you were at rest or during a specific movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any new hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in your ear during or after the episode? Also, do you have any history of migraines, recent head trauma, or other neurological conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the episode was so brief, did you notice any specific head movements that triggered the spinning, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? I also need to know if you have any history of high blood pressure or heart disease.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Electronystagmography (VNG) and Audiogram. Given your history of a sudden, brief spinning episode triggered by lying down without hearing changes, could you confirm if rolling your head to the side while lying down recreates that sensation?
